title: Progressive Revelation
definition: Progressive revelation is the truth that God revealed His redemptive plan over time with increasing clarity until its fulfillment in Christ.
summary: God unfolded His truth across history, bringing His promises to fullness in Jesus Christ.
christFocus: Jesus is the climax of God's revelation and the fulfillment of the promises, patterns, shadows, and hopes of Scripture.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Progressive revelation means God did not reveal everything at once. He spoke through promises, covenants, prophets, sacrifices, wisdom, history, and finally through His Son.

Later Scripture does not contradict earlier Scripture. It clarifies, fulfills, and deepens what God had already revealed. Christ brings the promises and patterns into their intended fullness.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Without progressive revelation, readers may flatten the Bible or misunderstand how the Old and New Testaments relate. This doctrine matters because it helps believers read Scripture as an unfolding story fulfilled in Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Read earlier Scripture with respect for its original setting and with awareness of how God later brings His promises to fulfillment in Christ. Let the whole Bible deepen your understanding.
